name: chumsky
description: Combinator library designed around error recovery and rich diagnostics; Pratt parsing, ariadne companion

approach.comment: Parser combinators written as Rust code; parsers are recursive descent with PEG semantics.

implementation.comment: Required deps are hashbrown, unicode-ident, unicode-segmentation (all pure Rust); optional stacker (default feature) is a Rust crate that uses psm/cc at build time — disable default features for a C-free tree.

repository.comment: Primary repo moved to Codeberg; the GitHub repo was archived on 2026-04-02 with a relocation notice.

documentation.comment: The guide (getting started, key concepts, error & recovery, recursion, debugging, technical notes, 'Foo' tutorial) is published inside the docs.rs API docs.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19. Version history is unusual: 1.0.0-alpha.0..alpha.8 (2023-2025) were followed by stable 0.10.0 (2025-03), 0.11.x, 0.12.0, 0.13.0 (2026-05-06). Research reflects 0.13.0.

grammar-class.comment: Combinators impose no formal class; the crate docs explicitly state parsers are recursive descent capable of parsing PEGs, and recover_with docs refer to PEG first-success semantics. README also claims context-sensitive grammars via the `extra::Context` mechanism.

left-recursion.comment: Pratt module (feature `pratt`) for operator expressions. Additionally `Parser::memoized` docs: 'Memoization also works with recursion, so this can be used to write parsers using left recursion' — opt-in per parser, hence `native` is qualified. README: left-recursion detection in debug mode.

ambiguity-handling.comment: PEG first-success semantics on `or`/`choice`; alternatives are tried with backtracking.

backtracking.comment: No cut/commit operator; Input trait supports checkpoint/rewind. `memoized` can bound the cost of repeated backtracking.

lexer-integration.comment: Scannerless over &str (Token = char) / &[u8]; also parses &[T] token slices, Stream/IterInput from any iterator. Guide's tutorial uses chumsky for both lexing and parsing; commonly paired with logos (dev-dependency in the repo).

precedence-pratt-support.comment: `chumsky::pratt` with infix/prefix/postfix and left/right/none associativity; behind the `pratt` Cargo feature.

unicode-aware.comment: &str input yields `char` tokens; `&Graphemes` input via unicode-segmentation; unicode-ident dependency for identifier parsing.

input-types.comment: Implementors: &str, &[T], &[T; N], Bytes (tokio `bytes` feature), Stream, IterInput, IoInput (seekable reader), MappedInput, WithContext, MappedSpan, &Graphemes. User-implementable Input trait. No rope/text-buffer input.

streaming-partial-input.comment: Stream/IterInput lazily pull tokens from an iterator but there is no nom-style Incomplete / 'need more' signal or resumable parse.

zero-copy.comment: README: 'Zero-copy parsing minimises allocation by having outputs hold references/slices of the input'; `Parser::to_slice` yields input slices.

span-tracking.comment: &str input uses SimpleSpan<usize> (offset range); Span trait has Offset and Context associated types, so custom spans (e.g. with file id) are first-class via WithContext/MappedSpan. No line/column computation built in — left to ariadne etc.

output-model.comment: Users build arbitrary Rust types via map/map_with.

semantic-actions.comment: map, map_with (span/state access), try_map, validate, foldl/foldr.

stateful-parsing.comment: extra::State / extra::Full thread mutable user state; SimpleState helper; map_with exposes state.

error-recovery.comment: `Parser::recover_with` takes a user-chosen Strategy: skip_until, skip_then_retry_until, via_parser (arbitrary recovery parser), nested_delimiters.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: ParseResult carries both an optional output and a Vec of errors; `validate` emits non-fatal errors.

expected-token-reporting.comment: error::Rich exposes `expected()` (RichPattern set) and `found()`; Simple/Cheap/EmptyErr trade this away for speed.

custom-error-types.comment: Error type is a generic parameter (extra::Err); users can implement the `Error` / `LabelError` traits.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Rich carries a span on every error plus labelled contexts (`contexts()`, `in_context(label, span)`) each with its own span.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: ariadne is by the same author; README and examples render diagnostics with it (dev-dependency ^0.5). No first-party miette/codespan bridge.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No tree reuse API; each parse is from scratch.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Output is user-defined; trivia is skipped by explicit combinators unless the user captures it.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: None of rust-analyzer/helix/zed/neovim depend on chumsky; downstream language servers (e.g. PRQL, Aiken) use it, but those are not the editors listed in the tag set.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: parse-rosetta-rs JSON benchmark (chumsky v0.12.0, rustc 1.94.1, checked 2026-09-19): chumsky 47 ms vs winnow 27 ms, peg 29 ms, lalrpop 40 ms, pest 62 ms, nom 68 ms. Suite has no hand-written reference parser, so the tier is relative to the fastest competitor (~1.7x winnow). README's own JSON bench claims parity with hand-written parsers but is maintainer-authored.

compile-time-impact.comment: Deep GAT-based generic types stress the trait solver; discussion #396 reports 40 s -> 4 min builds after a small change, fixed ~90x by `.boxed()` on large `or` chains. parse-rosetta-rs debug build 5 s vs winnow 1 s / nom 3 s (chumsky v0.12.0).

allocation-strategy.comment: Zero-copy slices, check-only mode, and EmptyErr/Cheap error types allow allocation-free parsing of slice inputs; Stream/IterInput and Rich errors allocate. Crate itself requires `alloc`.

generated-code-size.comment: Combinator library; no code generation. No source needed.

no-std-support.comment: `#![cfg_attr(not(any(doc, feature = "std", test)), no_std)]` with `extern crate alloc` — no_std + alloc when default features (std, stacker) are disabled.

unsafe-usage.comment: No forbid(unsafe_code). The Input trait's core methods (next_maybe, span, slice, ...) are `unsafe fn` with cursor-validity preconditions; ~31 `unsafe` occurrences in input.rs plus ~5 in lib.rs (Send/Sync impls for a phantom type). Precondition-based, no raw pointer/transmute tricks, but unsafe is part of the public extension API.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: No derive/attribute macros; optional `proc-macro` feature only adds trait impls for proc_macro2 token inputs.

dependency-count.comment: 0.13.0 required: hashbrown, unicode-ident, unicode-segmentation. Six more optional (stacker [default], regex-automata, lexical, either, serde, bytes, railroad, proc-macro2 per current main).

wasm-compatible.comment: Inferred: pure Rust, no_std+alloc capable, no build.rs. Not verified by a CI wasm target; disable `stacker` (default) for wasm32-unknown-unknown as it relies on native stack switching.

async-friendly.comment: `Boxed` parsers are backed by `Rc` and are !Send/!Sync; unboxed parsers are Send only if their closures are. No async input adapter — IoInput is a blocking BufReader.

github-stars.comment: GitHub mirror (archived 2026-04-02) as of 2026-09-19; the new Codeberg primary repo shows 104 stars.

maintenance-status.comment: Release 2026-05-06 and commits on Codeberg as recent as 2026-09-16. Project relocated GitHub -> Codeberg in April 2026; GitHub repo archived (do not read that as abandonment).

documentation-quality.comment: Multi-chapter guide + full-language tutorial + thorough API docs with examples and example projects; no dedicated migration guide from 0.9/1.0-alpha to 0.10+ found, so not a 5.

tutorial-book.comment: Guide includes 'Foo: A Tutorial' building a lexer, parser and interpreter.

notable-users.value: PRQL (prqlc-parser), Aiken smart-contract language, knuffel/knus KDL parsers, xee XPath engine
notable-users.comment: 306 reverse dependencies on crates.io (2026-09-19). logos is the top reverse dependency by downloads.

bus-factor.comment: zesterer 733 commits dominates; CraftSpider 173, Zij-IT 71, wackbyte 46, Hedgehogo 38. Three crates.io owners. Borderline solo.
